name: Input-noise stress test of the v3 SQL method on Superviz26-SQL
registered: 2026-11-27, after the Superviz26 primary test and after viewing the shape of benign training inputs (train split only, run 45936879185); before any perturbed row was scored or any stress model was fitted
question: Superviz26 benign inputs come from clean value pools. How much do benign alerts rise when some benign inputs carry realistic international values (names, street addresses, companies, cities with apostrophes, hyphens, commas, slashes and non-Latin scripts), and does learning from equally noisy training data restore a low alert rate without losing detection?
noise: Values come from Faker 37.12.0, whose per-locale providers hold real name, street and place lists. Locales: en_US, en_IE, fr_FR, de_DE, es_ES, pt_BR, tr_TR, pl_PL, vi_VN, ja_JP, zh_CN, ar_AA, hi_IN, sw. Kinds: name, street_address, company, city. A training pool (seed 2026112901) and a separate test pool (seed 2026112902), each 2,000 values per locale and kind (14 x 4 x 2,000 = 112,000 values); a value is drawn uniformly from the pool. A row is perturbed by replacing its first run of Latin-letter words (regex [A-Za-z][A-Za-z]+( [A-Za-z][A-Za-z]+)*) in user_inputs with a pool value. Rows with no such run are left unchanged and counted as not eligible. Attack rows are never perturbed.

arms.shock-a|b|c|d: The frozen indomain models (freeze b739c584, models from develop run 45928319914), unchanged. Every eligible benign test row is perturbed with the test pool. Reported: alert rate among perturbed benign rows, and the implied overall benign alert rate if 1%, 5% or 20% of benign traffic looked like this.
arms.matched-a|b|c|d-1|5|20: Refit with the unchanged procedure on lodo/x-x.csv train rows where each eligible row is perturbed with probability r (training pool, row draw seed 2026112903). Test rows: each eligible benign row perturbed with probability r (test pool, row draw seed 2026112904); attack rows unchanged. Reported: benign alert rate overall and among perturbed rows, attack detection, per technique.

expectations_registered: Shock: most perturbed benign rows alert in every domain, because apostrophes, hyphens, commas and slashes are new character classes for most templates (prediction: above 50%). Matched: benign alert rate returns near the 0.5% budget, and attack detection falls, because profiles that admit punctuation leave less room to flag injection.
pass_condition: For the matched arm at r = 5%, per domain B, C and D, both: benign alert rate at most 1% and attack detection at least 90%. Headline: domains passing out of 3. All other numbers are descriptive.
known_limits: Faker values are generated from real lists but are still generated; this measures sensitivity to a stated kind of input variety, not the false alarm rate on real users. Field boundaries inside user_inputs are unknown, so the replaced span may cover more than one field.
